_what: Results for the 15 candidate rows frozen in commit dc47e0d (favour-pack-candidates-2026-10-05.json). Both checks ran after the freeze. No row was edited after the freeze. A dropped row is a result.

_checks.a_aid: personalDataAsk(description) and safetyClauseProblem(safety) from src/lib/favour-safety.ts, run on all 15 at 05:09 CEST on 5 Oct. All 15 returned null on both. A control sentence in the same run ("Send a photo of your face and your home address.") was flagged, so the aid could say no in that run. The aid is weak evidence: on its frozen second set it caught 5 of 20 unsafe asks.
_checks.b_hostile_read: Read by the author, who also wrote the rows. For each row the author wrote the answer most likely to place the sender or expose someone. The test question: does an honest, literal answer to the row need something about the sender or about another person? If yes, the row fails. If the hostile answer has to be forced in against the question, the row passes. This is one reader with the author's blind spots. It is not an independent read.

_counts.note: See _pack_test for what the pack's own tests did to the 9 that were left.

results.hostileAnswer: We are still checking the photo of my front door that I sent.
results.why: The row asks for a rewrite of a posted sentence. The personal detail had to be forced in. An honest answer needs nothing about the sender.

results.hostileAnswer: Favour, because where I live we say do me a favour.
results.why: A pick and a reason about a name. The sender can volunteer where they live, but the row does not call for it. Note: Relay and Handy are also names of existing products. That is not personal data, but Oscar should know before posting.

results.hostileAnswer: Someone at the company will look at the passport photo I sent.
results.why: The row asks what the reader expects next. The detail had to be forced in.
results.heldBack: Held back by the author for a false note, not for a privacy reason. The row's whoWouldWantIt says the quoted message is the one 36 people got on the live app. Both parts are wrong. The live reason text is "AI verification error - proof flagged for manual review.", which is different wording. The live count was 36 of 44 claimed favours, not 36 people. The row was not edited after the freeze, so it is left out.

results.hostileAnswer: The sender reads the words "send a photo as proof" and sends a photo, of whatever is in front of them.
results.why: The row's own text contains the phrase "send a photo as proof". A hasty reader can take that as the instruction. A photo sent by mistake can show a face, a room or a screen. Whether the app's proof form takes a photo on a row like this is unverified. The row is dropped on the wording alone.

results.hostileAnswer: That you will sell what I write.
results.why: A doubt about a described product. Nothing about the sender is needed.
A word from the posted sentence and a replacement. A sender may add that the language is new to them, but the row does not ask.

An honest answer must name a language the sender can write. That is a fact about the sender, and the row says nothing about the sender is needed. For a small language it narrows where the sender is from to a small population. The row is dropped. The existing pack row translate-line asks for the same thing and has the same weakness. That row was read by four readers and is left as it is, with this weakness reported.

results.hostileAnswer: We could not accept this one. Please send it again.

results.hostileAnswer: Like claiming a refund on my insurance.

results.hostileAnswer: 10 now. Rent is due and I am short.
results.why: The row asks for a reason for wanting a reward sooner. The natural honest reason is the sender's own circumstances, often being short of something. It also reads like an offer of 15 points next week, which nobody has made.

results.hostileAnswer: Model and people checked it before points.
results.why: A shorter version of a posted sentence. Nothing about the sender is needed.
results.heldBack: Held back by the author, not for a privacy reason. The sentence to shorten says an answer was checked by a model and by people. On this board the check is the model alone, and the row's own checkedBy field says so. A reader of the board could take the quoted sentence as how the app works. The row was not edited after the freeze, so it is left out.

results.hostileAnswer: The first one, because the number I can still take is what I look for.

results.hostileAnswer: My bank's app locked me out last Tuesday, so I went to the branch near my flat.
results.why: The row asks for the sender's own experience. An honest, literal answer is a story from their life: which app, when, what they did. That can name a bank, a health or a dating service, a day and a place. The clause "nothing about you is needed" contradicts the ask. The aid did not catch this.
